correctness.rationale: The characteristic-three Newton identity and translation polynomial identity construct the cone; complete additive derivative classification over the algebraic closure gives precisely 15 singular lines and a unique vertex. A directly derived Hessian determinant 1 proves all base singularities are tame A1 nodes. Exhaustive finite-field enumerations yield Q(F3)=25 and Q(F9)=145. Fifteen split rational exceptional conics give Y(F3)=70, Y(F9)=280. K3 b2=22 and Weil equality at F9 force the squares of all eigenvalues to be 9; the first trace forces signs 21 positive, one negative. The exact zeta formula follows and has no unproved extension from a finite experiment.

originality.rationale: An exact mod-3 description and Frobenius-maximal K3 resolution were compared with the complex S6 pencil, the classical modular/tropical models, special-fiber exclusions, the general fifteen-nodal quartic theory and semantic published-finding searches. None of the inspected primary treatments supplies the specific all-extension arithmetic for the symmetric integral reduction. This is a qualified best-knowledge originality assessment, not proof of priority.
residual_risks: Early or unindexed characteristic-three geometry of the six-coordinate symmetric integral Burkhardt quartic may predate the cited modern literature.
F3 and F9 point-count tables for supersingular K3 surfaces could imply the spectrum if the precise surface is identified in them.
General fifteen-node geometry is known; no novelty is claimed for its abstract node count in unrelated surfaces.
Historic integral-model changes must not be taken as good reduction or a single canonical mod-3 fiber.

value.rationale: The exceptional characteristic-three fiber of the classical S6 symmetric Burkhardt quartic is not described by the usual characteristic-zero nodal theory or by the standard five-coordinate reduction. Its fifteen-line singular degeneration has intrinsic geometric motivation, and its 15-nodal K3 section unexpectedly saturates the Weil bound over F9. The exact Frobenius spectrum and zeta function are motivated arithmetic invariants of a classical moduli-related quartic, not an arbitrary numerical slice.
